EMERGENCY  /DISASTER

PLANNING/PROGRAMS  Following  the conclusion  of the Public  Hearing,  the City  Council
  unanimously  adopted  Resolution  No.  2024-69-CC  entitled  Resolution  of
  the City  Council  of the City  of South  Gate,  California,  adopting  the
  updated  Local  Hazard  Mitigation  Plan describing  the City's  efforts  to
  prepare  for and respond  to emergencies.

  ChiefArakawa  stated  Lieutenant  Camacho  will  be presenting  the item.

  Lieutenant  Camacho  stated  he is here as the City  of South  Gate's
  Emergency  Services  Manager  and gave  a presentation.

  Mayor  Hurtado  asked  if anyone  in the audience  wished  to speak  on this
  item  or if any emails  received.  Seeing  no one step forward  nor any emails
  received;  Mayor  Hurtado  closed  the audience  portion.

  Mr.  Camacho  stated  that this  item  does not address  the school  district
  directly  but we are in constant  contact  with  the school  district.

  Mayor  Hurtado  asked  how  the city  collaborates  with  the school  district  to
  address  these  issues.

  Councilwoman  Avalos  asked  how  many  staff  are in the EOC.  Are  we
  prepared  for any major  incidents.

CONT'D  Mr. Camacho  stated everyone  present  is a member  of the EOC team. And
  all city employees  bare responsibilities  to address the matter.

  Councilmember  Barron  asked how the collaboration  with  local  businesses

  is in case of an emergency.

  Mr. Camacho  stated not only through code enforcement  but building  and

  safety  and resources through the county are available.

  Councilmember  Barron  asked Ms. Elguira  if the city is including
  businesses  during  their  application  process  of what  type of materials  are

  being  housed  and what we require  as a city.

  Meredith  Elguira,  Director  of Community  Development  stated those types

  of conversations  are not held with  businesses  as they come in. She
  recommends  having  an informal  separately  asking the businesses if they
  are willing  to partner  with  the city.

  Vice Mayor  Davila  asked how the CERT  program  and the EOC works.

  Mr. Camacho  stated that CERT  is not part of the EOC.  CERT  is more for

  individuals  to take of their families  and neighbors.

  Councilmember  Rios has two concerns;  one regarding  schools  during  an

  emergency  and a business  with  chemicals.

  Chief  Arakawa  stated that this is a general  plan. Informing  the government
  we have a plan in place.

  Chief  Arakawa  also stated that all the chiefs  in the county  and sheriff  have

  had discussions  in case of emergencies.

  Staff's  recommendations  were unanimously  approved  by motion  of

  Council  MemberAvalos  and seconded  by Vice Mayor  Davila.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Barron,

  yes; Council  Member  Rios, yes; Vice Mayor  Davila,  yes; Mayor  Hurtado,
  yes.
